rules.problem: Covers every red-box item. Minor: 'Vaccination given' has no 'Recent' qualifier (see c033) and 'New ... asymmetric' is not expressed on the stroke signs (not expressible beyond Sudden onset).
The page's 'immediately before or during the collapse' / 'before the collapse' timing on the breathing and prodrome questions is not expressible in check_for; acceptable.

rules.rule: Measure lying and standing blood pressure after collapse/falls
rules.problem: Page asks 'systolic BP drop by >= 20 OR diastolic BP drop by >= 10'. Only a systolic-drop measurement is declared; there is no diastolic-drop measurement or finding, so the diastolic half of the page's test cannot be recorded. No SNOMED 'level of reduction in diastolic BP on standing' observable was found; the finding (snomed_concept "Postural drop in blood pressure" "finding") exists and could carry the Yes/No answer.
'consider stroke or TIA' -> possible, correct. Gated on collapse/falls as the page is.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible anaphylaxis after sudden collapse
rules.problem: 'check for anaphylaxis' -> possible, correct; and/or structure matches 'Sudden collapse and any of'. Allergen exposure lacks the 'past few hours' window (c095-c098).

rules.rule: Diagnose probable orthostatic hypotension after collapse/falls
rules.problem: Narrower than the page: the page's Yes branch is 'systolic drop >= 20 OR diastolic drop >= 10'; the rule only fires on the systolic drop, so a patient with an isolated diastolic drop >= 10 is never diagnosed and instead falls through to the hyperventilation / common faint branches.

The 'No' gate is (< systolic drop 20) only, so a diastolic drop >= 10 does not exclude this branch (c106). 'Hyperventilation likely' -> probable is right and Tachypnea/Excessively deep breathing match 'breathing very quickly or deeply'. Timing 'immediately before or during the collapse' is dropped (low).

rules.rule: Diagnose probable common faint after collapse/falls
rules.problem: Same incomplete 'No' gate on the BP-drop question (c112). Otherwise faithful: No to the breathing question as (no ...) pairs, Yes to any prodrome, 'Common faint likely' -> probable Vasovagal syncope.

Level Urgent matches 'Give urgent attention'; (and complaint (or ...)) structure matches. Problems: 'Vaccination given' with no recency makes any historically vaccinated adult who collapses Urgent (c158); allergen exposures lack the 'past few hours' window (c144-c147). Minor: footnote 2 defines 'shock likely' (SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness) which could be a probable Shock rule instead of a bare 'Shock' finding; the Pulse/glucose observables ('Pulse, function', 'Blood glucose status') exist but I could not confirm they are the house vitals concepts.
The page says 'Check Hb: if < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man), anaemia likely'. The brief requires every 'X likely' as a probable diagnosis; there is no Hb measure task and no anaemia rule in the file.

summary: Most consequential: the orthostatic hypotension rule and the 'No' gates of the hyperventilation and common faint rules use only the systolic drop (>= 20 / < 20) while the page asks 'systolic drop >= 20 OR diastolic drop >= 10', so an isolated diastolic drop is misrouted to the wrong branch and no diastolic-drop measurement exists. In the priority rule 'Vaccination given' has no recency (page: 'Collapse following vaccination') and the allergen exposures lack the footnote's 'past few hours' window. The page's 'anaemia likely' (Hb < 12 woman / < 13 man) is not encoded at all; everything else in the red box and the flowchart is encoded faithfully with existing SNOMED concepts.
